newsitem.title: EGYPT: Strategic investors eye Egypt china firm.
newsitem.headline: Strategic investors eye Egypt china firm.

text.p: Six investors are interested in buying up to 60 percent of Egypt's official Chini/General Pottery and China Products but they have yet to submit any formal offers, the agent for the sale said on Tuesday.
Nadir Ezzedin of the National Bank of Egypt (NBE) said Canadian, Egyptian and British investors were looking into the firm and now had up to September 30 to finally decide.
"They're all anchor investors and hopefully all six will give in bids," he said.
Ezzedin had said that the Canadian firm was willing to revamp Chini's technology but gave no details about the others.
The state initially put up at least 500,000 shares or 27.5 percent of Chini for auction but had said it was willing to sell 60 percent of its holding in the firm to a strategic investor.
It has so far extended the deadline for the sale twice.
Chini said it made a 1.69 million pound after-tax profit for the first nine months of the current financial year which began on July 1, 1995.
It did not provide comparative figures but said its after-tax profit for the whole of fiscal 1994/95 was 2.12 million pounds.
